purpose: Prove a CLOSED shadow root is OBSERVED - because the capture init script was in place before the component constructed itself - and that the surface is reported as observed rather than as a permanent blind spot. Before M3.2 this fixture asserted the opposite: that the walker was honestly blind here.
targeted_defect: Regression guard, re-aimed by M3.2 / T-FR-02. It previously pinned the anti-green-wash contract that an unreadable surface must become a named ledger row rather than an empty pass. That contract is unchanged and still binding - what changed is that this surface is no longer unreadable. `attachShadow({mode:'closed'})` hands its root to the component and to nobody else, so the ONLY moment it can be observed is the moment it is created; the hook is installed on the browser context, before any page script runs. A future change that installed it later - on the page, after navigation, or on demand - would silently restore the blind spot, and this fixture is what catches that.

expect_controls.why: The light-DOM control group: the ordinary page must read exactly as it did before the hook existed.

Inside the closed shadow root. Same frame, so no selector change - the compiler's getByRole/getByLabel pierce shadow DOM. Its name resolves via label[for] against the SHADOW ROOT, not the host document, because an id reference does not cross a shadow boundary.

opaque.why: OBSERVED, not opaque. Reporting a surface we read as a blind spot understates this crawl's coverage exactly as badly as the reverse would overstate it, so the row names what was read instead of what could not be.
